subject: Intermittent chunked-transfer stalls causing 504s — CTO briefing requested
messages:
From: Claire Harrington <claire@lumensys.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: Mohit Desai <mohit@lumensys.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:04 -0700
Subject: Re: demo environment - repeated 504s and streaming gaps

Naomi —

We started the live sandbox demo at 09:00 and around 09:07 we began seeing repeated 504s followed by long silent windows on the streaming output (clients see the connection up but no tokens for 6-12s). It kills the demo flow and causes timeouts in our orchestrator.

Symptoms we captured:
- Multiple clients showed token emission pauses of 6-12s, then a burst of tokens.
- Some requests returned 504 from the edge while backend accepted the request.
- The issue is intermittent; after a restart of the Edge Proxy the feed mostly recovered for ~30 minutes, then reoccurred.

Attached are the logs we collected (lumen_logs_20270427.tar.gz) and a short proxy trace (proxy-trace-20270427.txt). We can run another demo this afternoon if helpful but this is blocking our customer-facing test.

Can your team advise next steps? We need an ETA and whether this is likely a config/edge issue or runtime-facing problem. Our CTO will join a call if you think an executive sync is needed.

—Claire
Claire Harrington
Head of Integrations, LumenSys

I'll follow up with a short status update within 60 minutes.

Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:05:23 -07:00
Subject: Re: demo environment - repeated 504s and streaming gaps

Quick triage notes (preliminary):
- I ingested the proxy trace and backend logs from the bundle. There are repeated HTTP/1.1 chunked sequences where the edge finishes sending a chunked header but we see a 6-10s gap before the first payload chunk arrives at the downstream socket.
- The runtime shows the model worker continuing to produce tokens (KV cache advancing), but the token batches are batched in small groups and remain queued at the output layer. We see a backpressure signal from the proxy layer at 09:06:54 which coincides with the first 504s.
- Two hypotheses: (A) edge proxy buffer flush / TCP delayed ACK interaction causing periodic stalls, (B) an intermittent scheduler stall on the worker causing production bursts.

Next actions I will run now:
- Enable per-connection debug logs on the edge for Claire's IP range (short window).
- Pull p95/p99 token emission timings from the worker for the last 24h and correlate to proxy logs.

Attaching short extract: proxy-trace-20270427.txt (you already have). I will post a follow-up with timing graphs.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 13:12:47 -07:00
Subject: CTO briefing requested: LumenSys demo — streaming stalls and cascading 504s

Team —

Short summary for exec/board visibility: LumenSys (POC customer, OPP-3472) reported an interruption during a live demo resulting in repeated 504s and token emission gaps (6–12s). We've reproduced the pattern in traces; initial analysis shows chunked-transfer gaps with tokens buffered at the worker output. Impact: demo failure and potential near-term churn risk if not resolved quickly.

What we have so far:
- Customer-provided logs and proxy traces (attached).
- Rishi's initial triage: chunked header handshake completes, then a multi-second gap before payload chunk arrives; worker appears to be producing tokens but they are not flowing steadily to the client.

Immediate asks:
- Engineering (Jonas/Rishi): please prioritize a 2-hour deep-dive root-cause and mitigation plan. Focus areas: edge buffer/tcp interactions, keepalive/timeout tuning, and worker scheduler fairness. If we can provide a temporary config (edge keepalive/buffer adjustments) we should prepare a safe rollback path.
- Sales/CS (Vanessa): join the customer call at 14:00 PT and coordinate messaging; prep an internal CS playbook (one-liner for the CTO).
- Execs (Aditya cc'd): request a brief sync at 15:00 PT if the 2-hour triage identifies a customer-experience risk requiring cross-team decisioning (credits, SLA exception).

I will consolidate the 60/120 minute updates in this thread. Attaching the Drive link and HubSpot ticket HS-28934 for context.

Thanks — urgent on this.
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Claire Harrington <claire@lumensys.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Thanks Naomi — we appreciate the quick escalation and the proposed 14:00 repro. 14:00 PT works; our CTO can join briefly if you want the executive-level context.

For the repro: we'll spin up a load that mirrors our demo orchestrator (six concurrent clients, ~1.2k token/session). We'll capture packet-level tcpdump as well in case this is mid-path related.

If you surface a config-based mitigation that reduces the 6–12s silent windows (even as a temporary setting), that will buy us time for a full fix. We'll be on the call.

—Claire
